title: Classes, prototypes and the prototype chain

videos.script:
Make an empty array. {{empty}} It has no properties of its own, and yet you can call map on it, and filter, and push. Where do they come from?

From another object. {{proto}} Every object in JavaScript has a hidden link to one other object, its prototype. When you ask for a property the object does not have, the language follows that link and asks the prototype. And the prototype has a prototype of its own, all the way up to a single object at the top. That path is the prototype chain.

{{classes}} Classes, which you will use in every framework after this course, are built on top of that chain. The class syntax arrived in 2015, and it is a cleaner way to write what the language was already doing with functions and prototypes. Today you will see both, so that neither one is magic.

{{inherit}} Then inheritance: one class extending another, and what super means. {{private}} And private fields, the hash sign, which finally lets a class keep something to itself.
